parts:
It looks like alpha_phi, beta_phi, gamma_phi, delta_phi, lluce, and llambda are parameters, not transformed parameters, so you should move them from one block to the other.

You should also declare the constraints on those parameters as real<lower=-3,upper=3>… rather than just as real…, and then I think you can drop the truncation on the sampling statements.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Large number of errors when attempting to run code and I'm not sure what to do.
parts:
If you are using rstan you can use extract() to extract samples from a model 

model1 <- stan(file="my_model.stan",  init =my.inits(), pars =my.params, data=my.data,  warmup = 200, iter= 2000, chains = 4)
output1 <- extract(model1, permuted = TRUE)   

output1 will be an array and you can access the parameters by calling them by their name

output1$mean

or

output1$sd

the function print() will return you a table containing  a resume of the model

print(model1)

or if you want only to check one parameter:

print(model1, pars="mean", probs=c(0.5, 0.025, 0.975), digits=3)

Hope that help

Chris
-------------

> All of these rejections are due to the fact that the constraints on the parameters and the constraints on the transformed parameters are not compatible. If lambda is a transformed parameter that must be <= 10, then whatever parameter(s) get transformed into lambda have to be constrained to make that happen. For example, if the parameter were lambda_squared, then it would need to be constrained to be <= 100.
